outcomes: Laboratory studies used sound timed to measured brain activity.
Reported memory findings differ between studies.
The app delivers no stimulation and predicts no memory or recovery benefit.

education.limitations: Early laboratory research is not routine advice. The preset values do not reproduce a study protocol or establish a personal benefit.

sources.title: Papalambros et al. (2017): acoustic stimulation study
sources.population: 13 cognitively healthy adults aged 60–84; one stimulation and one sham night.
sources.supports: EEG-timed sound pulses were studied for sleep rhythms and word recall.
sources.limitations: Small laboratory crossover study. Whole-night slow-wave activity was similar; interval effects and recall findings do not establish home-use benefit or brain clearance.

sources.title: Henin et al. (2019): acoustic stimulation replication
sources.population: 12 healthy adults in a nap experiment and 19 in an overnight experiment; inclusion ages 18–30.
sources.supports: Sleep-rhythm changes were observed without better performance on the tested memory tasks.
sources.limitations: Different tasks and protocols limit generalisation. Results do not establish a reliable memory benefit or an insomnia treatment.
